chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan ibn Aban narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated to us from his brother al-Hasan, from Zur'a ibn Muhammad, from al-Mufaddal ibn Umar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

My father (peace be upon him) used to separate the fasts of Shaban and the month of Ramadan by one day, and Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) used to connect them (fast continuously), and he would say: 'Fasting for two consecutive months is a repentance from Allah.'

key_terms.شَعْبَان: Shaban (the eighth month of the Islamic calendar)

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between the fasting practices of Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn and his father regarding Shaban and Ramadan?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Thawab al-A’mal* illustrates the scholarly principle of *Ikhtilaf* (divergence) among the Imams, where differing practices are both valid rather than contradictory. While Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn (Zayn al-Abidin) connected Shaban and Ramadan to emphasize the merit of continuous fasting as expiation, the variation highlights the flexibility in devotional acts within Shia jurisprudence. The specific emphasis on 'two consecutive months' serves as a theological basis for the virtue of maintaining spiritual momentum across the transition from the month of preparation to the month of revelation.
